description: Curated set of well-known human genes with GRCh38 coordinates

genes.name: Tumor Protein P53
genes.description: Tumor suppressor gene; most frequently mutated gene in human cancers. Encodes a transcription factor that regulates cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, and DNA repair.

genes.name: BRCA1 DNA Repair Associated
genes.description: Tumor suppressor involved in DNA double-strand break repair. Mutations significantly increase risk of breast and ovarian cancer.

genes.name: BRCA2 DNA Repair Associated
genes.description: Involved in homologous recombination repair of DNA. Mutations increase risk of breast, ovarian, pancreatic, and prostate cancers.

genes.name: Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor
genes.description: Transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase. Frequently mutated or amplified in non-small cell lung cancer, glioblastoma, and other cancers.

genes.name: KRAS Proto-Oncogene GTPase
genes.description: GTPase involved in cell signaling. Activating mutations found in pancreatic, colorectal, and lung cancers.

genes.name: MYC Proto-Oncogene
genes.description: Transcription factor regulating cell growth and proliferation. Amplified or overexpressed in many cancers.

genes.name: APC Regulator Of WNT Signaling
genes.description: Tumor suppressor gene. Mutations cause familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) and are common in sporadic colorectal cancers.

genes.name: Phosphatase And Tensin Homolog
genes.description: Tumor suppressor that negatively regulates the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Frequently mutated in many cancer types.

genes.name: RB Transcriptional Corepressor 1
genes.description: First tumor suppressor gene identified. Regulates cell cycle progression. Mutations cause retinoblastoma and are found in many cancers.

genes.name: B-Raf Proto-Oncogene
genes.description: Serine/threonine kinase in the RAS-MAPK pathway. V600E mutation is common in melanoma, thyroid, and colorectal cancers.

genes.name: PI3K Catalytic Subunit Alpha
genes.description: Catalytic subunit of PI3-kinase. Frequently mutated in breast, endometrial, and other cancers.

genes.name: Erb-B2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinase 2
genes.description: Also known as ERBB2. Receptor tyrosine kinase amplified in ~20% of breast cancers. Target of trastuzumab (Herceptin).

genes.name: ALK Receptor Tyrosine Kinase
genes.description: Receptor tyrosine kinase. Gene fusions (especially EML4-ALK) are oncogenic drivers in non-small cell lung cancer.

genes.name: Von Hippel-Lindau Tumor Suppressor
genes.description: Tumor suppressor involved in ubiquitin-mediated degradation of HIF. Mutations cause Von Hippel-Lindau disease and clear cell renal carcinoma.

genes.name: CF Transmembrane Conductance Regulator
genes.description: Chloride channel gene. Mutations cause cystic fibrosis, the most common lethal genetic disease in Caucasians.

genes.name: Huntingtin
genes.description: CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion in this gene causes Huntington's disease, a progressive neurodegenerative disorder.

genes.name: Hemoglobin Subunit Beta
genes.description: Beta-globin gene. Mutations cause sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia.

genes.name: Insulin
genes.description: Encodes preproinsulin. Mutations can cause neonatal diabetes. The INS locus is also associated with type 1 diabetes susceptibility.

genes.name: Apolipoprotein E
genes.description: Lipoprotein involved in cholesterol metabolism. The APOE4 allele is the strongest genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease.

genes.name: Amyloid Beta Precursor Protein
genes.description: Precursor to amyloid-beta peptide. Mutations cause early-onset familial Alzheimer's disease. Duplication causes Down syndrome-related dementia.

genes.name: Superoxide Dismutase 1
genes.description: Antioxidant enzyme. Mutations cause familial amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

genes.name: Fragile X Messenger Ribonucleoprotein
genes.description: CGG trinucleotide repeat expansion silences this gene, causing Fragile X syndrome, the most common inherited form of intellectual disability.

genes.name: Dystrophin
genes.description: Largest known human gene (2.2 Mb). Mutations cause Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy.

genes.name: Forkhead Box P2
genes.description: Transcription factor involved in speech and language development. First gene linked to a speech disorder.

genes.name: Sex Determining Region Y
genes.description: Master switch for male sex determination. Encodes a transcription factor that triggers testis development.

genes.name: Telomerase Reverse Transcriptase
genes.description: Catalytic component of telomerase. Reactivation is a hallmark of cancer. Promoter mutations are common in many tumor types.

genes.name: Tumor Protein P63
genes.description: Member of the p53 family. Essential for limb and epithelial development. Mutations cause ectodermal dysplasia syndromes.

genes.name: Cadherin 1 (E-Cadherin)
genes.description: Cell-cell adhesion glycoprotein. Germline mutations cause hereditary diffuse gastric cancer. Loss promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition.

genes.name: Janus Kinase 2
genes.description: Tyrosine kinase in the JAK-STAT pathway. V617F mutation is the hallmark of myeloproliferative neoplasms.

genes.name: BCR Activator Of RhoGEF And GTPase
genes.description: Fusion partner in the BCR-ABL1 (Philadelphia chromosome) translocation. BCR-ABL1 drives chronic myeloid leukemia.

genes.name: ABL Proto-Oncogene 1
genes.description: Non-receptor tyrosine kinase. BCR-ABL1 fusion protein is the target of imatinib (Gleevec) in CML treatment.

genes.name: Fibroblast Growth Factor Receptor 3
genes.description: Receptor tyrosine kinase. Activating mutations cause achondroplasia (most common form of dwarfism) and are found in bladder cancer.

genes.name: MutL Homolog 1
genes.description: DNA mismatch repair gene. Germline mutations cause Lynch syndrome (hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer).

genes.name: MutS Homolog 2
genes.description: DNA mismatch repair gene. Along with MLH1, mutations cause Lynch syndrome and microsatellite instability in tumors.

genes.name: ATM Serine/Threonine Kinase
genes.description: DNA damage response kinase. Mutations cause ataxia-telangiectasia and increase cancer susceptibility.

genes.name: Cyclin Dependent Kinase Inhibitor 2A
genes.description: Encodes p16INK4a and p14ARF tumor suppressors. One of the most frequently deleted genes in human cancers.

genes.name: Neurofibromin 1
genes.description: RAS-GAP tumor suppressor. Mutations cause neurofibromatosis type 1, one of the most common genetic disorders.

genes.name: Neurofibromin 2 (Merlin)
genes.description: Cytoskeletal linker protein. Mutations cause neurofibromatosis type 2, characterized by bilateral vestibular schwannomas.

genes.name: WT1 Transcription Factor
genes.description: Zinc finger transcription factor. Mutations cause Wilms tumor (childhood kidney cancer) and are involved in leukemia.

genes.name: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor A
genes.description: Key regulator of angiogenesis. Target of bevacizumab (Avastin). Tumor angiogenesis is a hallmark of cancer.

genes.name: Isocitrate Dehydrogenase 1
genes.description: Metabolic enzyme. R132H mutation produces oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate. Common in gliomas and AML.

genes.name: Platelet Derived Growth Factor Receptor Alpha
genes.description: Receptor tyrosine kinase. Mutations and amplifications found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) and glioblastoma.

genes.name: KIT Proto-Oncogene Receptor Tyrosine Kinase
genes.description: Stem cell factor receptor. Activating mutations drive GIST, mastocytosis, and some melanomas and leukemias.

genes.name: Ret Proto-Oncogene
genes.description: Receptor tyrosine kinase. Germline mutations cause multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN2). RET fusions found in thyroid and lung cancers.

genes.name: SMAD Family Member 4
genes.description: Central mediator of TGF-beta signaling. Tumor suppressor lost in pancreatic and colorectal cancers.

genes.name: Catenin Beta 1
genes.description: Key component of the WNT signaling pathway. Activating mutations found in hepatocellular carcinoma and other cancers.

genes.name: Glucosylceramidase Beta
genes.description: Lysosomal enzyme. Mutations cause Gaucher disease and are the most common genetic risk factor for Parkinson's disease.

genes.name: Leucine Rich Repeat Kinase 2
genes.description: Kinase/GTPase. G2019S mutation is the most common genetic cause of Parkinson's disease.

genes.name: Hexosaminidase Subunit Alpha
genes.description: Lysosomal enzyme. Mutations cause Tay-Sachs disease, a fatal neurodegenerative disorder.

genes.name: Phenylalanine Hydroxylase
genes.description: Enzyme converting phenylalanine to tyrosine. Mutations cause phenylketonuria (PKU).

genes.name: Methylenetetrahydrofolate Reductase
genes.description: Enzyme in folate metabolism. C677T variant is associated with elevated homocysteine and neural tube defect risk.

genes.name: Cytochrome P450 2D6
genes.description: Key drug-metabolizing enzyme. Highly polymorphic; affects metabolism of ~25% of drugs including codeine, tamoxifen, and antidepressants.

genes.name: Presenilin 1
genes.description: Component of gamma-secretase complex. Most common cause of early-onset familial Alzheimer's disease (>300 mutations known).

genes.name: Sodium Voltage-Gated Channel Alpha Subunit 1
genes.description: Neuronal sodium channel. Mutations cause Dravet syndrome and other epilepsy syndromes.

genes.name: Notch Receptor 1
genes.description: Transmembrane receptor in the Notch signaling pathway. Activating mutations in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia; loss-of-function in squamous cell carcinoma.

genes.name: MET Proto-Oncogene Receptor Tyrosine Kinase
genes.description: Hepatocyte growth factor receptor. Amplification and mutations drive several cancer types including lung and renal.

genes.name: NRAS Proto-Oncogene GTPase
genes.description: RAS family GTPase. Mutations common in melanoma, acute myeloid leukemia, and thyroid cancer.

genes.name: Raf-1 Proto-Oncogene
genes.description: Serine/threonine kinase in the MAPK pathway. Germline mutations cause Noonan syndrome. Fusions found in some cancers.

genes.name: Survival Of Motor Neuron 1
genes.description: Essential for motor neuron survival. Homozygous deletion causes spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), the leading genetic cause of infant death.

genes.name: Dual Specificity Tyrosine Phosphorylation Regulated Kinase 1A
genes.description: Kinase involved in brain development. Located in the Down syndrome critical region. Overexpression contributes to intellectual disability in trisomy 21.

genes.name: Angiotensin Converting Enzyme 2
genes.description: Receptor for SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. Entry point for COVID-19 infection. Also regulates the renin-angiotensin system.
